newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor says owns all of Alusaf aluminium.
newsitem.headline: Gencor says owns all of Alusaf aluminium.

text.p: Gencor Ltd said on Monday that its offer to Alusaf minority shareholders had been accepted and it now owned 100 percent of the aluminium concern.
Last month Gencor announced it had lifted its stake in Alusaf to 73 percent by buying the state-run Industrial Development Corporation's 32 percent interest.

"I am pleased to tell you today that offer to minorities was accepted and Gencor now owns 100 percent of Alusaf," Gencor chairman Brian Gilbertson said on Monday at a presentation of the group's results for the year ended June 30.
He said Alusaf would generate strong cash flows and that Gencor would have "sole access to those strong cash flows and that has been one of our objectives for a number of years".
Gencor had also consolidated its position in aluminium producer Billiton in the year under review.
The group's aluminium division was the largest contributor accounting for 34 percent of operating income from 37 percent the previous year, Gilbertson said.

The division benefitted from the build-up at Alusaf's Hillside smelter. The last pot was commissioned at Hillside on June 21, some five months ahead of schedule, and Gencor said it was not clear capacity would approach 500,000 tonnes a year, rather than the originally planned 466,000 tonnes.

"Over the course of three or four years we have managed to grow that aluminium business from that old Bayside smelter (at Alusaf)...to one of the world's significant aluminium businesses. We are probably number five in the world now. It has been a very satisfactory process," Gilbertson said.
